narrative.coaching_note: Wash your hands with soap and water before you touch resident A, that is the one change to make next time. At 22 seconds your gloved hand touched bed rail A and picked up C. difficile spores, and at 26.3 seconds those spores moved from your glove to call button. You then touched resident A at 55.2 seconds without the cleaning before touching that was needed. The alcohol rubs you used at 0.2, 32.3 and 64.1 seconds do not kill C. difficile spores, so use soap and water and wash for the full 40 seconds instead. Next time wash with soap and water right after you take gloves off and right before you put gloves on.
narrative.audit_summary: For C. difficile, source was bed rail A. Transfer chain: bed rail A to gloved hand at 22 seconds, then gloved hand to call button at 26.3 seconds. One Moment 1 opportunity before gloved hand touched resident A at 55.2 seconds was missed; compliance 0 met over 1 opportunity, overall 0/1. Three alcohol rubs at 0.2, 32.3 and 64.1 seconds met WHO duration at 21.8, 22.9 and 24.2 seconds but were not effective against this pathogen; soap and water that clears spores would work. Glove use showed no effective hygiene before donning at 54.8 seconds and after doffing at 32.3 seconds. No resident exposures occurred. End contamination included bare hand, gloved hand, bed rail A and call button. Disinfect call button and bed rail A with an EPA List K sporicidal disinfectant effective against C. difficile spores.
narrative.top_fix: The highest-impact single change in this clip was effective hand hygiene for Moment 1 before touching resident A at 55.2 seconds.
